doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Moving to the U.S. and great Canadian artists
summary: Shaffer says coming to the U.S. seemed a fantasy and happened through fortuitous circumstances; he discusses Canadian stars.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Wow did it seem obvious that you needed to go to the United States eventually?

Well yes. It seemed like a fantasy though, very difficult, I was aware, to do, to get the kind of credentials you needed to work legally in the U.S. as a Canadian. But it wasn’t like it is today. Certainly we look at today’s musical artists and we see that some of the top, absolute top tier musicians and performers are Canadians. Drake, you know? Need I © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
say more? And The Weeknd. Both Torontonians. It wasn’t like, Celine Dion, my goodness, we look at some of the huge impactful artists. In my day we had Lightfoot, Gordon Lightfoot, The Guess Who.

Yes, thank you, certainly Joni Mitchell, yes. But she had her impact after she moved to Los Angeles and that, you know, I would never have done it on my own, come to the U.S. I certainly didn’t come here and say here I am, you know, how do I get started. Again, it was just a series of crazy fortuitous — right place at the right time things that brought me here.
